tests.name: Numerical Reasoning Test 12
tests.subtitle: AssessmentDay · Test 12
tests.description: A 30-question mixed-difficulty numerical reasoning test using online vs high street sales, European company sales, Gills & Tines Ltd financials, team timesheets, Deus Bank fund and bond sales, and assets/liabilities data.
tests.instructions:
This numerical reasoning test comprises 30 questions, and you will have 30 minutes in which to correctly answer as many as you can. Calculators are permitted for this test, and it is recommended you have some rough paper to work on.

You will have to work quickly and accurately to perform well in this test. If you don't know the answer to a question, leave it and come back to it if you have time. Each question will have five possible answers, one of which is correct. You may click Back and Next during the test to review or skip questions.

You can submit your test at any time. If the time limit is up before you click submit the test will automatically be submitted with the answers you have selected. It is recommended to keep working until the time limit is up.

Try to find a time and place where you will not be interrupted during the test. The test will begin on the next page.

questions.prompt: What are the combined sales of quarters 1 and 4?
questions.explanation: Quarter 1 = 21% and Quarter 4 = 30% of £1,675,000. Combined share = 51%. 0.51 × £1,675,000 = £854,250. Answer C.

questions.prompt: If the profit margin for online sales is 1/8th of the sales value, what was the total profit for online sales in 2009?
What is the difference in sales between the best and worst performing quarters?
questions.explanation: Best quarter = Quarter 4 (30%); worst = Quarter 1 (21%). Difference = 9% of £1,675,000 = 0.09 × £1,675,000 = £150,750. Answer D.

questions.prompt: What was the difference between Online and High Street sales (in £10,000s)?

In 2010 there is a High Street CD and DVDs sale that results in an increase in the annual 2009 sales of each category by 11% and 14.5% respectively. What are the combined High Street DVD and CD sales for 2010?
questions.explanation: "Respectively" maps CDs to +11% and DVDs to +14.5%. High Street CDs 2009 = 28.9 × £10,000 = £289,000 → × 1.11 = £320,790. High Street DVDs 2009 = 29.0 × £10,000 = £290,000 → × 1.145 = £332,050. Combined = £652,840. Answer C. (Reversing the percentages gives £652,805, which is not an option.)

questions.prompt: In which quarter did Sclics plc, Farlaz and Raik Ltd each experience an increase in sales for the European Region?
questions.explanation: Quarter-on-quarter changes (£m): Q1→Q2 Sclics 5.0→4.4 (down), Farlaz 7.2→5.8 (down), Raik 5.3→5.8 (up); Q2→Q3 Sclics 4.4→4.8 (up), Farlaz 5.8→5.1 (down), Raik 5.8→6.2 (up); Q3→Q4 Sclics 4.8→3.5 (down), Farlaz 5.1→6.4 (up), Raik 6.2→6.3 (up). Quarter 1 has no earlier 2009 quarter to compare against. No quarter shows an increase for all three companies. Answer E.

questions.prompt: If the annual European sales for Raik Ltd represent 45% of worldwide sales, what is the level of sales worldwide?
questions.explanation: Raik Ltd annual European sales = 5.3 + 5.8 + 6.2 + 6.3 = £23.6 million (the projection bar is excluded). Worldwide = 23.6 ÷ 0.45 = £52.444 million ≈ £52.4 million. Answer B.

questions.prompt: How much did Sclics plc’s European sales in quarters 1 and 2 differ from Farlaz’s European sales over the same period?
questions.explanation: Sclics plc Q1 + Q2 = 5.0 + 4.4 = £9.4 million. Farlaz Q1 + Q2 = 7.2 + 5.8 = £13.0 million. Sclics sold 13.0 - 9.4 = £3.6 million less. Answer B.

questions.prompt: If the annual sales target for Raik Ltd was £29.5 million, by what fraction of this target did the company underperform?
questions.explanation: Raik Ltd annual sales = 5.3 + 5.8 + 6.2 + 6.3 = £23.6 million. Shortfall = 29.5 - 23.6 = £5.9 million. 5.9 ÷ 29.5 = 0.2 = 1/5. Answer B.

questions.prompt: Next quarter’s total sales projection represents what increase on Quarter 4’s total sales for the three companies shown (to the nearest whole %)?
questions.explanation: Quarter 4 total = 3.5 + 6.4 + 6.3 = £16.2 million. Next quarter projection total = 3.2 + 7.4 + 6.6 = £17.2 million. Increase = 1.0 ÷ 16.2 = 6.17%, which is 6% to the nearest whole %. Answer E. (6.2% in option C is the one-decimal value, but the question asks for the nearest whole %.)

What was the total number of days spent on Client work in March using the formula 1 day = 7 working hours (to the nearest whole day)?
If there were 3 members within Team B, what was the average number of hours spent on non-client work during March?
questions.explanation: Team B non-client hours = Admin 42 + Training 6 + Meetings 72 = 120. Per member = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 hours. Answer D.

questions.prompt: If Teams A-C bill clients at £75 per hour and less experienced Teams D and E bill clients at £55 per hour, what is the total client income for March (to the nearest £1,000)?

If the monthly summary shown is representative of the time typically spent each month over the course of a year (1 year = 12 months) then how many days (1 day = 8 working hours) do Teams A-E spend in meetings over the course of a year?
questions.explanation: Monthly meetings = 40 + 72 + 32 + 18 + 56 = 218 hours. Annual = 218 × 12 = 2616 hours. Days = 2616 ÷ 8 = 327 days. Answer A.

questions.prompt: Put the teams in increasing order of total hours worked in March (starting with the lowest number of total hours worked).

questions.sectionTitle: Deus Bank new institutional investor and private client sales
questions.prompt: What is the ratio of Fund P’s sales to new private clients compared to new institutional investors?
questions.explanation: Fund P private client sales = $2,500; Fund P institutional sales = $17,500. 2,500 : 17,500 = 1 : 7. Answer D.

questions.sectionTitle: Deus Bank new institutional investor and private client sales
questions.prompt: What are Deus Bank’s total new private client and institutional investor Fund sales (in £s) at an exchange rate of $1.55 to the £?
questions.explanation: Fund sales only (Funds P, F and G): institutional 17,500 + 21,000 + 23,000 = $61,500; private 2,500 + 2,250 + 1,600 = $6,350. Total = $67,850. At $1.55 per £: 67,850 ÷ 1.55 = £43,774.19 ≈ £43,774. Answer E. (Option C, £80,677, is all sales including bonds: $125,050 ÷ 1.55.)

questions.sectionTitle: Deus Bank new institutional investor and private client sales
questions.prompt: Deus Bank pays 6% and 8% commission on Bond U and Bond S sales respectively over $15,000. How much commission is paid for new Bond U and Bond S sales (across both private clients and institutional investors)?
questions.explanation: Combine both client types as instructed. Bond U = 29,000 + 1,750 = $30,750; amount over $15,000 = $15,750 × 6% = $945. Bond S = 24,000 + 2,450 = $26,450; amount over $15,000 = $11,450 × 8% = $916. Total commission = $945 + $916 = $1,861. Answer E. (Applying the threshold to institutional sales alone gives $840 + $720 = $1,560, option C, which ignores the 'across both' instruction.)

questions.sectionTitle: Deus Bank new institutional investor and private client sales

What was the approximate fraction of Fixed Assets to Loans Made at the end of the financial year 2009?
Which asset or assets have changed in value by more than 12% from 2007 to 2009?
questions.explanation: 2007→2009 changes: Liquid Assets 10,735 → 10,214 = -4.85%; Loans Made 21,974 → 24,600 = +11.95%; Derivatives 513 → 512 = -0.19%; Fixed Assets 542 → 614 = +13.28%. Only Fixed Assets exceeds 12% (Loans Made is just under at 11.95%). Answer D.

questions.prompt: In 2010, Loans Made are projected to decrease by an eighth and both Derivatives and Fixed Assets are projected to increase by 5%. If other values stay the same what will be the impact on the 2010 Total Assets value (in £million)?
questions.explanation: Using 2009 values as the base: Loans Made change = -24,600 ÷ 8 = -3,075.0; Derivatives change = 512 × 5% = +25.6; Fixed Assets change = 614 × 5% = +30.7. Net change = -3,075 + 25.6 + 30.7 = -3,018.7, i.e. a 3,018.70 decrease. Answer B.

questions.prompt: Which liability or liabilities have experienced a 10% change in value between 2008 and 2009?
questions.explanation: 2008→2009 changes: Reserve Liabilities 124.0 → 111.6 = -10.0%; Borrowings 1,544.0 → 1,389.6 = -10.0%; Share Liabilities 1,628.0 → 1,958.0 = +20.27%; Other Liabilities 35.0 → 41.8 = +19.43%. Exactly 10% changes: Borrowings and Reserve Liabilities. Answer B.

questions.prompt: What is the ratio of Reserve Liabilities (2008); Reserve Liabilities (2007)?
questions.explanation: Reserve Liabilities 2008 = 124.0; 2007 = 132. 124 : 132; dividing both by the HCF of 4 gives 31 : 33. Answer D.
